content:
maria: quick q on API error semantics for /v1/generate — when should we return 4xx vs 5xx? specifically: malformed JSON vs semantic validation (prompt too long / disallowed tokens) vs transient infra (GPU OOM) vs rate limit. also: how should SDKs detect whether an error is retryable?

aj: short answer: 4xx = client problem that won't succeed without change; 5xx = server/transient. some specifics:
- 400 = bad JSON / missing required top-level fields
- 401/403 = auth/perm
- 422 = semantic validation (e.g., prompt violates constraints or length)
- 409 = conflict/duplicate request (idempotency violation)
- 429 = rate limit / quota exceeded (retryable with backoff)
- 503 = temporary capacity issues (retryable)

sam: i'd add that GPU OOM should map to 503 (or 507?) but 5xx is fine and mark as transient. 507 is uncommon, stick to 503 so SDKs don't misinterpret.

leo: on the "retryable" signalling part — we debated whether to add a boolean in the body ("retryable": true) vs relying on status codes + headers. my vote: prefer standard headers (Retry-After) + codes. body boolean can be a helpful hint but not required.

infra-bot: infra note: we emit Retry-After for 429 and 503 when we can estimate recovery. we also set X-Request-Id on all responses.

maria: +1. a concrete proposal:
1) Malformed JSON -> 400, body {error: {code: "malformed_json", message: "..."}}
2) Schema/semantic validation -> 422, code like "validation_error", include field-level details array
3) Rate limits -> 429 + Retry-After, code "rate_limit"
4) Transient server/resource (OOM, short infra outage) -> 503 + Retry-After when possible, code "temporary_unavailable"
5) Duplicate idempotent request -> 409 with code "conflict" and include conflicting request id

Also propose we include an optional "retryable" boolean in error body for ambiguous cases (e.g., model-specific runtime errors) so SDKs can be simpler. example error body we could standardize to in openapi: 

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_error",
    "message": "Prompt exceeds max tokens",
    "details": [{"path": "prompt", "reason": "too_long", "max": "8192"}],
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

aj: that JSON looks good. two notes: 1) keep codes machine-friendly (snake_case), 2) don't overuse retryable: SDK should primarily trust status code + Retry-After. fallback to body boolean only if present.

sam: for backward compatibility: older clients might expect 400 for all validation. when we roll out 422 we should accept both in server-side routing (i.e., don't change semantics for existing clients) and add compatibility tests. also announce in changelog.

maria: i'll update the openapi and add a set of unit tests + a small migration guide. can someone review the PR when i open it? @aj @sam

aj: will review, aim to do it tomorrow morning.

leo: i'll add an e2e that asserts Retry-After present on simulated capacity fails.

maria: thanks! also quick question: should SDK automatically retry once for 503/429 with exponential backoff, or leave to app?

aj: SDK should do one transparent retry for idempotent calls (and only if Retry-After absent or small). otherwise expose a helper retry util and document recommended policy (exponential with jitter).

sam: +1. document default: max 2 retries, base backoff 200ms, max 5s. keep it conservative to avoid cascading load.

maria: perfect. i'll draft the PR with those defaults and link to this thread. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: FYI, we'll also emit metrics for 4xx vs transient 5xx so ops can tune autoscale and dedicated fallback rules.

maria: noted, thanks everyone. assigning follow-ups in the PR.
